messages.text:
Hi Sarah,

Here is what I have:

Power Supply ONE
1. Power 30.3 W to 30.4 W It fluctuates between these two wattages.

2, Input Voltage 4.8 V to 5.0 V. I have seen it drop down to 4.7 V.

I have had to adjust this power supply twice over the course of several
hours. Both times it was adjusted to 5.1 V but it dropped back down to
these numbers after a few hours and kept fluctuating between the 4.8V to 5V.

Power Supply TWO
1. Power 30 W to 31 W It fluctuates between these two Wattages.

2. Input Voltage 4.8 V to  5 V. It fluctuates between these two Voltages.

This one was adjusted to 5.1 V but dropped back down to between the 4.8 V
to 5 V. This one was only adjusted once.

Power Supply THREE
1. Power 28.5 W

2. Input Voltage 5.1 V This one does NOT flucuate at all.

I adjusted this one to 5.1 It has stayed at the 5.1 V but the wattage now
only shows 28.5 W. This power supply also is the only one that does NOT
flucuate on either the POWER or the INPUT VOLTAGE.

So in essence I have two power supplies that I have made adjustments to as
per your request that still fluctuate between 4.8 V to 5 V Input Voltage
while the Power fluctuates a bit also.

Power supply three is the only one that has stayed at the 5.1 V on a
consistant basis while its Power now only reads 28.5.

If there is any more testing or adjustments you would like me to try, let
me know.

Thanks,
Chuck
Note to the team: Handed to Hal.

Hi!

I'm happy to say that all three have been behaving pretty well. Only ONE of
the readings is sitting at 4.9 V now. The other two are showing 5 V I know
you said the voltage readings are not useful, but I am happy they are not
bouncing around like they have been. The power on #1 has dropped to 28.4 V

It seemed to me all wires were clamped pretty tight but I tightened them up
about an eighth of a turn just to make sure.

As far as I can tell none of them threw a power fault or rebooted. All of
them are in different rooms of my house.

The temps for each one is:

1. Hashrate 1.84 Th/s
    ASIC Temperature 51 °C
    Voltage Regulator Temperature 52 °C
    Power 28.4 W
    Input Voltage 5 V
    ASIC Frequency 900 MHz
    Measured ASIC Voltage 1.2 V
    BCH Solo Mining

2. Hashrate 1.77 Th/s
    ASIC Temperature 53°C
    Voltage Regulator Temperature 52 °C
    Power 31 W
    Input Voltage 5 V
    ASIC Frequency 900 MHz
    Measured ASIC Voltage 1.2 V
    BTC Solo Mining

3. Hashrate 1.99 Th/s
    ASIC Temperature 56 °C
    Voltage Regulator Temperature 56 °C
    Power 31.2 W
    Input Voltage 4.9V
    ASIC Frequency 900 MHz
    Measured ASIC Voltage 1.2 V
    BTC Solo Mining

If you need or want me to do anything else..I'll do my best to get it done.

Chuck

Hi Chuck,

That all reads like three healthy units. 1.77 to 1.99 TH/s at 900 MHz is right where a Bitaxe Gamma should sit, ASIC temps in the low to mid 50s with the regulators tracking alongside them is comfortably in range, and no faults or reboots across a full day of running is the number that actually mattered. The input voltage settling at 4.9 to 5.0 instead of bouncing is a good sign too, that is the tighter terminals doing their job.

On the 28.4 W on unit one, that is watts rather than volts, and a little variation between boards is normal. Each chip has its own efficiency, so one drawing 28 W while another pulls 31 W at the same frequency and the same 1.2 V is just silicon lottery. Nothing to chase there, and unit one is actually your most efficient of the three.

So nothing more to do. Leave the V.ADJ screws where they are, keep them running, and only come back to us if one throws a power fault or reboots on its own. Thanks for doing all that testing properly, it is what let us find the real answer instead of swapping parts.

When you do get to that bigger unit, just ask and I will walk you through what fits your power and space.

It was a pleasure helping you with this. If you were happy with how we handled it, a review on Trustpilot would mean a lot to us: https://www.trustpilot.com/review/heliumdeploy.com . You are also very welcome in our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf for new products and hands-on help.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy Support

Hi Sarah,

Sorry to bother you with this again, but one of them has done a power fault.

I have attached an image showing it for you.What should I do next?
Note to the team: Handed back to Hal.

Ok. It is NOT the first one that threw the fault. That original fault was
with the one I call BitaxeT.

The one that just now threw the fault I call BitaxeC2.

The first image, 3720, is showing the ORIGINAL power fault  (BitaxeT) AND
the image I just sent (BitaxeC2) in one pic. BOTH of these are two
different power supplies. The B. has not thrown a fault since that
time.

The B.2 is the one with the power fault

I just now swapped between those two units and now my BitaxtT is showing
the fault.now. This is being shown in image 3721.

I hope I explained it properly.

Chuck
Note to the team: Handed to Hal.

Hey Hal,

Its been seven days now and I have not heard anything back from anyone yet.
Can you check into this for me?

Thanks,
Chuck
Handed to the team · PSU-only warranty replacement needs a person to ship the part; no tool on my sid

Hi Chuck,

You are right to chase, and I am sorry. Hal finished the diagnosis a week ago and nothing came back to you after that. That wait is on us, not on you, especially after all the testing you did to pin it down.

Where it actually stands: the swap test settled it. The fault follows that one power supply, so it is a single bad Mean Well LRS-50-5 and not a bad Bitaxe. Your units are covered, and because it is the supply and not the miner, there is nothing for you to send back. The replacement supply is what you need, and I have put the request for it in front of the team with everything Hal recorded, so they do not have to ask you for any of it again.

They are offline right now and pick this up tomorrow at 10am Eastern. The reply comes straight to this address, so you do not need to watch for anything tonight.

In the meantime, leave the faulty supply unplugged and keep the other two units running as they are. The idle Bitaxe is fine sitting switched off. If either of the running two throws a fault before you hear back, just reply here with what the Swarm page shows.

Thanks for your patience on this one, Chuck.

Sarah, HeliumDeploy Support
